es: Escribir una escena de recuerdo en primera persona con detalles sensoriales y verbos de memoria con gerundio o infinitivo (remember, forget, regret).

teaching.en: I remember playing on my grandmother's porch every summer, long before I understood how rare those carefree afternoons would turn out to be.
teaching.es: Recuerdo haber jugado en el porche de mi abuela cada verano, mucho antes de entender lo raras que serían aquellas tardes despreocupadas.
teaching.explanationEs: Remember + -ing es el recuerdo de algo que ya ocurrió: me veo jugando en el porche.

understood how rare those carefree afternoons would turn out to be.

teaching.en: I must remember to call her on Sunday, because last month I forgot to ring on her birthday and she has never mentioned it since.
teaching.es: Tengo que acordarme de llamarla el domingo, porque el mes pasado olvidé llamar el día de su cumpleaños y ella nunca lo ha mencionado desde entonces.
teaching.explanationEs: Remember + to es no olvidar una tarea futura; forgot to + verbo indica que no hiciste algo por olvido.
segments: I must remember to call her on Sunday, because last month I forgot
to ring on her birthday and she has never mentioned it since.
teaching.audioText: I must remember to call her on Sunday, because last month I forgot to ring on her birthday and she has never mentioned it since.

teaching.en: I will never forget hearing the creak of that old gate, a sound that can still evoke the whole summer in a single second.
teaching.es: Nunca olvidaré oír el chirrido de aquella vieja verja, un sonido que todavía puede evocar todo el verano en un segundo.
teaching.explanationEs: Forget + -ing es un recuerdo vivido que no se borra; creak añade un detalle sonoro y evoke lo que despierta.
segments: I will never forget hearing the creak of that old gate, a
sound that can still evoke the whole summer in a single second.
teaching.audioText: I will never forget hearing the creak of that old gate, a sound that can still evoke the whole summer in a single second.

teaching.en: I regret not saying goodbye to her properly, and when I look back on that evening, I wish I had stayed a little longer.
teaching.es: Lamento no haberme despedido de ella como es debido, y cuando miro atrás a aquella tarde, desearía haberme quedado un poco más.
teaching.explanationEs: Regret + -ing lamenta algo que hiciste o no hiciste; not va delante del -ing; look back on = recordar un periodo pasado.
segments: I regret not saying goodbye to her properly, and when I look
back on that evening, I wish I had stayed a little longer.

teaching.en: The scent of warm bread used to linger in the hallway, and it is still the most vivid memory I have of that house.
teaching.es: El olor del pan caliente solía quedarse en el pasillo, y sigue siendo el recuerdo más vívido que tengo de aquella casa.
teaching.explanationEs: Scent, warm y vivid son detalles de los sentidos; linger es quedarse en el aire mucho después.

it is still the most vivid memory I have of that house.

teaching.en: An echo of her voice still stays in my mind, which shows how a single detail can bring back an entire scene.
teaching.es: Un eco de su voz todavía permanece en mi mente, lo que demuestra cómo un solo detalle puede devolver una escena entera.
teaching.explanationEs: Echo añade un detalle sonoro y lo une con la memoria: still marca que el recuerdo sigue ahí.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que cuenta un recuerdo vivido, no una tarea pendiente.

choices.text: I remember swimming in the river until sunset every August.
I remembered to swim in the river until sunset every August.
I regret to swim in the river until sunset every August.

feedback.es: Remember + -ing cuenta algo que ya ocurrió; remembered to habla de una tarea y regret to + verbo no expresa un recuerdo.

hint.es: Un recuerdo de algo vivido lleva el verbo de memoria seguido de -ing.

origin.text: Mia asks Leo about the summers he spent in his grandfather's village, and he answers with a vivid memory.

prompt.es: Completa: «Olvidé cerrar la ventana antes de salir…»

feedback.es: Forget + to significa que no hiciste algo por olvido: no cerraste la ventana.

hint.es: Es una tarea que no se hizo: el verbo de memoria va seguido de to.

origin.text: I forgot ___ the window before leaving, so the rain ruined the carpet while we were away.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Nunca olvidaré oír el chirrido de aquella vieja verja.»

answer.text: I will never forget hearing the creak of that old gate

feedback.es: Never forget + -ing recuerda algo vivido; the creak of that old gate añade el detalle sonoro.

hint.es: Empieza por I will never forget y sigue con el -ing.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige de qué se arrepiente quien habla.

choices.text: Not having returned to the sea after so many years.
Not having thanked the aunt for those summers.
Having spent too many summers away from home.

feedback.es: «I regret not thanking her» indica que lamenta no haberle dado las gracias a su tía por aquellos veranos.

origin.audio: Every summer we stayed at my aunt's house by the sea. I can still smell the sea and the warm bread she baked on Sunday mornings. I remember running along the beach at sunrise, and I will never forget the creak of the wooden steps under my feet. Years later I regret not thanking her for those weeks, and I must remember to visit her when I am next in town.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué tarea pendiente menciona quien habla.

choices.text: Baking the same bread for her own family.
Calling the aunt every Sunday morning.
Visiting the aunt the next time she is in town.

feedback.es: «I must remember to visit her» es una tarea futura: visitar a su tía la próxima vez que esté en la ciudad.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué da a entender sobre la relación con la madre.

choices.text: That the speaker wishes they had said thank you more often.
That the speaker and the mother are no longer in contact.
That the mother never wanted to live above a bakery.

feedback.es: «I regret not saying how much it all meant» muestra que quien habla querría haber dado las gracias más a menudo.

origin.audio: I spent most of my childhood in a small flat above a bakery. Even now, the scent of warm bread can bring that whole time back: the creak of the stairs, the echo of my mother's voice from the kitchen. I regret not saying how much it all meant to me, and I sometimes wonder whether she ever knew.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige con qué propósito menciona la escalera y el eco de la voz.

choices.text: To complain about how noisy the old flat used to be.
To show how one scent can bring the whole past back.
To explain why the family moved out of the flat.

feedback.es: El olor del pan arrastra detalles de oído (la escalera, el eco): muestra cómo un solo sentido reabre todo el pasado.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cuando miro atrás a ese verano, lo primero que recuerdo es el olor del pan.»

feedback.es: Look back on es la colocación para recordar un periodo pasado con perspectiva.

origin.text: When I ___ back on that summer, it is the scent of warm bread that comes to mind first, before the faces or the words.

prompt.es: Escribe la escena de recuerdo que se pide en el recuadro.

answer.text: I remember standing on my grandmother's porch on hot summer evenings, when the air was warm and heavy and the scent of fresh bread drifted out of the kitchen. I can still hear the creak of the old gate and the echo of my cousins laughing in the garden. I will never forget watching the sun go down behind the hills while she told us stories about her own childhood. One evening I forgot to say goodbye when my parents took me home, and I still regret not hugging her that night. When I look back on those summers, I realise how much they shaped me. Now I must remember to call her every Sunday, because the scent of bread alone is not enough to keep a voice alive. Some memories linger for ever, small and golden, exactly as they were.
accepted: I remember standing on my grandmother's porch on hot summer evenings, when the air was warm and heavy and the scent of fresh bread drifted out of the kitchen. I can still hear the creak of the old gate and the echo of my cousins laughing in the garden. I will never forget watching the sun go down behind the hills while she told us stories about her own childhood. One evening I forgot to say goodbye when my parents took me home, and I still regret not hugging her that night. When I look back on those summers, I realise how much they shaped me. Now I must remember to call her every Sunday, because the scent of bread alone is not enough to keep a voice alive. Some memories linger for ever, small and golden, exactly as they were.

I remember playing in my grandfather's garden every summer, long before I understood how rare those days were. The air was warm, and the scent of ripe apples was everywhere. I can still hear the creak of the wooden gate and the echo of his voice calling us in for dinner. I will never forget eating under the big tree while he told funny stories about his youth. I regret not asking him more questions about his life, and I must remember to visit his house again this year. When I look back on those evenings, I realise that the smallest details are the ones that stay with me. Even now, when I close my eyes, that garden comes back, small and green and full of light. It is a vivid memory, and I do not want to forget it.

feedback.es: Una escena de recuerdo combina primera persona, detalles de los sentidos y verbos de memoria con -ing o to según lo que recuerdes o lamentes.

origin.text: Escribe en inglés una escena de recuerdo de un lugar de tu infancia, por ejemplo la casa de tu abuela (entre 140 y 230 palabras). Cuenta en primera persona, añade detalles de olor, sonido o tacto y usa al menos tres estructuras: remember + -ing, forget/regret + -ing y remember/forget + to.

prompt.es: Lee el fragmento. ¿Qué sugiere que la autora solo enumere los objetos del padre?

choices.text: That the author prefers lists to telling any personal story at all.
That the father left little behind and was easily forgotten.
That a loss can be conveyed through concrete details rather than statements.

feedback.es: Los objetos concretos (el abrigo, la taza, la carta) transmiten la pérdida sin nombrarla: emoción mediante detalles.

origin.text: In her memoir, the author never describes her father's face. She only lists the things he left behind: a coat that still carried his scent, a cup with a crack in it, a letter he never finished. She never says that she misses him.

prompt.es: Completa: «Nunca olvidaré ver caer la primera nieve en el porche…»

feedback.es: Never forget + -ing recuerda algo vivido: ver caer la nieve es una experiencia que no se borra.

origin.text: It was a quiet winter, and I will never forget ___ the first snow fall on the porch, and the silence that followed.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué actitud muestra la hablante hacia la memoria de su madre.

choices.text: Curious, but she expects her mother may not remember either.
Certain that her mother remembers every detail of that day.
Not interested in who took the photo or in why it matters.

feedback.es: Quiere preguntar, pero sospecha que su madre dirá que lo ha olvidado: curiosidad con poca esperanza.

origin.audio: I remember finding the old photo in a drawer last spring. The colours were pale now, but I could still feel how warm that afternoon had been. I must remember to ask my mother who took it, although I suspect she will say she has forgotten.
